header: DO NOT EDIT: regenerate with `python3 proofs/verus/gen_pin_tests.py <spec> --run`.
Each test mirrors one [pins] row of proofs/verus/affix_strip_fold_sync.txt and
drives the REAL pass (`affix_strip_fold::transform` / `expr`), not a copy of it.
The value rows do not stop at the node shape: they read the folded node's
`pattern`/`prefix`, apply it to a concrete value with Rust's own
`strip_prefix`/`strip_suffix`, and compare with what BASH prints for
That makes the two rows the manifest used to leave UNMIRRORED -- the no-match
value and the single-occurrence value -- executed evidence rather than a claim.

pins.note: Proof: for a magic-free literal the shortest and the longest matching prefix are the same one, so `#` and `##` are one strip. Source: both ops fold to the SAME AffixStrip and bash prints the same string for both.
Proof: fold_preserves_value -- the node's strip_prefix is bash's `${v#lit}`. Source: the folded node evaluated on a value equals bash's output, including a literal LONGER than the value (no match).
Proof: fold_preserves_value_suffix -- the same law at the back of the value. Source: java accepts the AffixStrip branch, and its value equals bash's `${v%lit}`.

Proof: star_forms_preserve_value -- `#lit*` is `#lit` and `%*lit` is `%lit` (the shortest match is the literal itself). Source: the star shape folds to AffixStrip(body) and bash prints what the literal op prints.

Proof: the four find/rfind identities are distinct nodes; `##*X` is not `#*X`. Source: `#*X` folds to CutAt(head=false, first=true) and `##*X` to (head=false, first=false), and bash prints `bX` vs the empty string.

cases.note: `${p%/*}` -- the CutAt string identity, not GNU dirname

pins.note: Proof: the two-argument path spellings are the same cut identities. Source: they fold to those CutAt nodes.

pins.note: Proof: the empty-body star family keeps each op's verified meaning. Source: each of the three arities folds to its own node.
Proof: the boundary of the literal branch -- a one-character literal is a literal. Source: it folds, so an off-by-one in the length gate would show here.
Proof: a pattern with glob magic is not a literal strip (`lit_free` false), and the EMPTY pattern is outside `0 < p.len()`. Source: both are left untouched.
Proof: `##lit*` / `%%*lit` are the conditional-strip shapes the star table does not cover. Source: refused on every target.

The row that used to be UNMIRRORED. Proof: `bash_prefix_strip`/`bash_suffix_strip` leave the value alone when no prefix/suffix matches. Source: the folded node applied to a value with no occurrence returns the value, and bash agrees.

The row that used to be UNMIRRORED. Proof: literal_strip_is_one_occurrence -- at most ONE occurrence goes. Source: with the literal appearing twice, the folded node removes exactly one, and bash prints the same.
Proof: fold_t_covers -- the visit reaches every depth, a forgotten call-argument arm goes red. Source: a strip inside an `echo` argument folds.
Proof: single_star_shape requires the star at an END. Source: a middle star is refused (the glob engine is required).
Proof: no_hard_magic -- `?`, `[`, `\` in the star BODY would make glob match diverge from a find cut. Source: refused.
Proof: fold_t's op gate -- only the four strip ops are sites. Source: the substitute ops are left alone.
